partneringMinimumAge.citation: The age of majority, at which a person marries without a parent's consent in nearly every state; the youngest age the game pairs.

partneringPeakAgeWomen.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Table MS-2, 'Estimated Median Age at First Marriage, by Sex: 1890 to Present' (CPS ASEC): women's median age at first marriage, 2022.

partneringPeakAgeMen.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Table MS-2, 'Estimated Median Age at First Marriage, by Sex: 1890 to Present' (CPS ASEC): men's median age at first marriage, 2022.

partneringAgeSpread.citation: Years from the median age at first marriage over which the pull of one's age fades (first marriages spread over roughly ages 20 to 40, and remarriage later).

partneringAgeGapSpread.citation: Years of age difference between partners over which the pull fades; U.S. Census Bureau, America's Families and Living Arrangements (CPS ASEC 2022), Table FG3: most married couples are within five years of each other's age.
partneringAgeGapSpread.estimatedFrom: Census CPS ASEC 2022 Table FG3 age difference of spouses; spread 4 to 7

partneringClosenessWeight.citation: How far a close tie pulls two people toward marrying, against the pull of staying as they are.

partneringAgeWeight.citation: How far being near the usual age at first marriage pulls toward marrying.

partneringGapWeight.citation: How far an age gap between two people pulls against their marrying.

partneringTemperamentWeight.citation: How far a person's temperament (every trait's lean toward committing over keeping things as they are, from the shared trait table) moves the choice.

partneringStayPull.citation: The pull of staying as one is, calibrated so marriages among a town's full people run near the national rate (CDC/NCHS National Vital Statistics System, provisional number of marriages and marriage rate, United States, 2000-2022: 6.2 marriages per 1,000 total population in 2022).

partneringMarriageRate.citation: CDC/NCHS National Vital Statistics System, provisional number of marriages and marriage rate, United States, 2000-2022: 6.2 marriages per 1,000 total population in 2022. The check, never a draw.

partneringCourtshipPerMonth.citation: How much a month of courting adds, per unit of how well two people suit each other, toward the pull of staying as they are; calibrated so marriages among a town's full people run near the national rate (CDC/NCHS NVSS, 6.2 marriages per 1,000 population in 2022).

partneringIntroductionWeight.citation: How close two people introduced by a mutual friend start out, as a share of the two ties that link them. Meeting through friends is one of the main ways American couples meet (Rosenfeld, Thomas and Hausen 2019, PNAS 116(36):17753, How Couples Meet and Stay Together 2017: about 20% of heterosexual couples who met in 2017, down from about a third earlier).

partneringIntroductionHours.citation: Hours two people introduced by a friend spend together when they first meet: an evening out.
partneringIntroductionHours.estimatedFrom: An evening's social time; ATUS 2023 socializing and communicating on days people do it is about 2 to 3 hours.

partneringAcquaintanceLevel.citation: How close two people who know each other by name but have no recorded tie (a classmate, a coworker) count when courting begins, on the 0-to-1 closeness scale.

partneringFaithWeight.citation: How far belonging to a faith pulls a couple to marry before living together.

partneringMarryAgeWeight.citation: How far being older than the usual age at first marriage pulls a couple to marry before living together.

partneringMoveInStayPull.citation: The pull of moving in together first rather than marrying, calibrated to the share of first marriages preceded by living together. Measured: 72% of new couples move in together first, against 76% of first marriages preceded by living together (NCFMR from NSFG, 2015-2019).

partneringWeddingPerMonth.citation: How much a month of living together adds toward marrying, per unit of the couple's closeness, against the pull of staying as they are; calibrated so marriages in all stay near the national rate. Measured over eight drawn towns: 0.08 gave 7.6 marriages per 1,000 with couples already living together marrying about 30% a year; 0.06 brings that near 22% (NSFG: 40% of first cohabitations marry within three years, NHSR 64).
